key_insight: Introducing a lightweight Persistent Visual Memory (PVM) module that maintains accessible visual representations so LVLMs retain visual perception throughout long autoregressive generation, counteracting visual attention decay.
problem_solved: Addresses 'Visual Signal Dilution'—the loss of effective visual attention as textual history grows in autoregressive LVLMs, which weakens visual grounding during long multimodal generation.
method: Quantify and diagnose visual signal dilution in autoregressive LVLMs (attention to visual tokens decays as generated text length increases).
Introduce a lightweight, learnable Persistent Visual Memory that stores and supplies sustained visual features in parallel to the model's language pathway.
Integrate PVM as an on-demand visual retrieval pathway so visual cues remain strong across long-generation sequences while keeping the module parameter-efficient.
impact: Enables more robust long-form, visually grounded generation and dialog in LVLMs by preserving vision-language alignment over long contexts—useful for multimodal assistants, narration, and complex visual QA.
visual_elements: Line chart: attention-to-visual-token strength vs. generated sequence length showing decay (before) and stabilized curve (after PVM).
Block diagram: LVLM architecture with a parallel PVM module that stores and supplies visual features to the generator.
Side-by-side example: a long image-grounded dialog or caption sequence with and without PVM highlighting differences in visual consistency.
Attention heatmaps: per-token visual attention across a long generation demonstrating dilution vs. persistent attention with PVM.
paper_title: Persistent Visual Memory: Sustaining Perception for Deep Generation in LVLMs
paper_authors: Siyuan Huang, Xiaoye Qu, Yafu Li, Tong Zhu, Zefeng He
